title: Rollout Traffic Orchestrator: client-side safety hooks, idempotent gateway, and auto-rollback primitives
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We need a compact, production-safe API/SDK surface that lets customers run canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and shadow traffic with automatic rollback triggers. Current primitives are scattered: orchestration-level traffic manifests, console-only rollouts, and ad-hoc client helpers. This ticket scopes the engineering work to a coherent gateway + client helper set that enforces idempotency, RBAC, and decision observability while enabling auto-rollback based on health signals.

Goals / success criteria:
- New public endpoint(s) to submit and update rollout plans programmatically (create, patch traffic split, promote, pause, abort).
- Client helpers (JS/Go) that encapsulate idempotent operations, optimistic concurrency (ETags), audit metadata, and decision explainability hooks for SDK consumers.
- Shadow traffic primitive that forwards a copy of live requests to a trial model without affecting response paths, with sampling and privacy controls.
- Auto-rollback triggers based on configurable health metrics (error-rate, latency p95, quality-regression signal) with a safe rollback strategy and audit trail.
- RBAC scopes and permission checks: rollout:create, rollout:mutate, rollout:promote, rollout:view, rollout:abort; SDK should surface clear authorization errors.
- Observability: per-rollout telemetry (traffic splits, exposure, anomalies), and integration points for Console metrics and Alerting rules.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Idempotency: use an explicit idempotency_key header for create/update operations plus server-side dedupe window (24h) and an eventual consistency model for traffic reconciliation. We avoid implicit auto-increment IDs to prevent replay hazards.
- Concurrency: apply ETag-based optimistic locking on rollout manifests. Updates that fail ETag check return 409 with a canonical read link so clients can reconcile. This favors availability and simplicity over complex transactional workflows.
- Auto-rollback action model: rules are declarative (monitoring expression + threshold + window + scope) and evaluated by the control plane. We will start with in-memory short-term decisions and a durable incident record for audit. Full transactional rollback across multi-region deployments is scope-gated for later phases.
- Shadow traffic privacy: by default we scrub PII from shadowed requests and provide an opt-in that preserves richer payloads for authorized experimenters. This adds slight compute overhead but is necessary for compliance.

API sketch (examples):
- POST /v1/rollouts => create rollout manifest (idempotency_key header recommended)
- GET /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id} => fetch manifest + status + exposures
- PATCH /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/traffic => adjust splits {route: percentage} (requires rollout:mutate)
- POST /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/promote => promote canary to steady-state (requires rollout:promote)
- POST /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/abort => abort + rollback to previous stable model (requires rollout:abort)
- POST /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/shadow => enable/disable shadow forwarding, sampling rate config
- GET /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/history => timeline of events and triggers

SDK helpers (JS/Go):
- helpers.createOrGetRollout(manifest, idempotencyKey) => idempotent creation pattern; returns { rolloutId, etag }
- helpers.patchTraffic(rolloutId, splits, etag) => apply change with optimistic lock; retries after fetch when 409
- helpers.waitForPromotion(rolloutId, successCriteria, timeout) => polls status and surfaces rollback reason if auto-rollback triggered
- helpers.shadowClient.wrap(request, opts) => transparently emit shadow copies with configurable scrubbing and metric labels

Acceptance tests and QA:
- unit tests for idempotency window and duplicate request dedupe
- integration tests simulating concurrent patches to validate ETag 409 flow and client retry behavior
- E2E simulation: deploy a canary that increases error rate -> expect control plane to detect threshold breach and trigger abort + emit audit event and rollback action
- Shadow traffic correctness: ensure sample percentages match exposure logs and that scrubbed payloads do not leak PII in logs

Operational concerns and rollout plan for this feature:
- Phase 1 (beta): API + JS SDK helpers + server-side idempotency and ETag; enable in a single region behind feature flag; Console shows experimental rollout view.
- Phase 2: Go SDK, shadow privacy controls, auto-rollback tuning and alert wiring; add telemetry hooks for cost estimation.
- Phase 3: cross-region consistent rollback, RBAC fine-grain roles, and formal SLAs for rollout action latency.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we implement a transaction log for rollouts to support time-travel debug? Trade-off: stronger debugging at cost of storage and complexity.
- Exact semantics for idempotency_key expiration and user guidance for long-running rollouts.
- How to expose quality-regression signals from Redwood Optimize into the control plane as a first-class metric.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MLOps/Rollout+Traffic+Orchestrator
- API contract draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/api/rollouts/draft
- Draft Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_mockups
- Relevant PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4216 (ETag scaffolding), https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/802 (shadow helper prototype)

Progress log and next steps:
- 2025-02-06: Spike completed implementing ETag flow in a playground service (Maya). Observed 3x fewer conflict retries in synthetic workload.
- 2025-02-18: Security reviewed shadow scrubbing approach; recommended default opt-out of full payload retention (security comment attached).
- 2025-02-25: PR for idempotency dedupe window merged to staging (PR #4216).
- Next: Implement public POST /v1/rollouts endpoint and JS SDK helper createOrGetRollout. Coordinate with Console team for experimental UI hook (PM: Aisha Rao).

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- POST /v1/rollouts supports idempotency_key and returns consistent resource when retried within dedupe window.
- PATCH /v1/rollouts/{id}/traffic enforces ETag optimistic lock and returns 409 with canonical resource link on conflict.
- Shadow forwarding primitives available in SDK with default PII scrubbing enabled and sampling control.
- Auto-rollback rule evaluation triggers recorded incident and produces rollback action within configured window in >95% of test runs.
- RBAC checks in place; unauthorized actions return 403 with scope hint.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the idempotency dedupe window and auditability requirements. If we choose too long a dedupe window we risk stale operations; too short and clients may see duplicate resources from retries behind flaky networks. We plan to expose the dedupe TTL in the API documentation so SDKs can surface guidance to developers.
